title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
hints: this is the general version of the single-transaction and unlimited-transaction stock problems - what extra piece of state do you now need to track that you didn't before?

for each allowed transaction count j from 1 to k, track two running values as you scan the days: the best profit if you're currently holding a share after using at most j buys, and the best profit if you're not holding one after using at most j complete transactions
buy[j] on a given day is the better of: staying in the same holding state from yesterday, or buying today using yesterday's sell[j-1] as your starting cash
sell[j] on a given day is the better of: staying in the same non-holding state from yesterday, or selling today from yesterday's buy[j]
the final answer is sell[k] after processing all days; also consider capping k at n/2 up front, since you can never use more than that many profitable transactions
commonMistakes: not capping k when it's larger than half the number of days, causing unnecessary work or, in incorrect implementations, wrong answers
mixing up the order of updates for buy[j] and sell[j] within the same day, accidentally using today's buy[j] to compute today's sell[j] when yesterday's value was intended, or vice versa
forgetting the base case buy[j] must start as able to buy on day 0 (i.e. initialized to -prices[0]), not zero
treating this as k independent single-transactions problems solved separately, which double counts or misses interactions between transactions
not handling k = 0 or an empty/single-day prices array as trivial zero-profit cases

content.problemStatement:
You're given an integer `k` and an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a stock on day `i`. You may complete at most `k` transactions, where each transaction is one buy followed later by one sell.

**Find and return the maximum total profit achievable with at most `k` transactions.**

You must sell the stock before you can buy again, so you can only hold at most one share at a time.
notes: k = 0 (no transactions allowed, profit is always 0)
prices is empty or has only one day (no transaction is possible)
prices strictly decreasing the whole time (best answer is 0, never trade)
k is larger than the number of profitable trades actually available (extra transactions simply go unused)

sampleTestCases.explanation: buy on day 0 at price 2, sell on day 1 at price 4, for a profit of 2. only one transaction is used, which is within the limit of at most 2
buy at 2, sell at 6 (profit 4), then buy at 0, sell at 3 (profit 3), total profit 4 + 3 = 7, using exactly 2 transactions
buy at 1, sell at 6, profit 5, the best single transaction available

optimal.time: O(n * k) where n is the number of days and k is the transaction limit
optimal.space: O(k), since only the previous day's buy/sell arrays are needed at each step
optimal.pattern: dynamic programming with a state machine of buy[j] and sell[j] for j = 1..k, tracking the best profit achievable after at most j transactions while currently holding a share (buy[j]) or not holding one (sell[j])

bruteForce.approach: recursively try, on every day, all three choices (buy, sell, or do nothing), tracking how many transactions have been used so far, and take the best outcome across all decision paths
bruteForce.time: O(3^n) - exponential, revisits the same (day, transactions used, holding) states repeatedly
